To align the caption of a table to the left in LaTeX without using the `caption` package, you can use the `\caption` command with the `[l]` (left-align) option or redefine the caption formatting using basic LaTeX commands.

### **Method 1: Using `\caption[l]{...}` (if supported)**
Some document classes (like `article`) allow left alignment directly in the `\caption` command:
```latex
\begin{table}[h]
  \centering
  \begin{tabular}{l c r}
    Left & Center & Right \\
    1 & 2 & 3 \\
  \end{tabular}
  \caption[l]{This is a left-aligned caption.}
\end{table}
```
*However, this does not work in all LaTeX distributions, so check if it works for you.*

### **Method 2: Redefine `\@makecaption` (Manual Approach)**
If the above doesn't work, you can patch the internal `\@makecaption` command to left-align captions:
```latex
\makeatletter
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \sbox\@tempboxa{#1{#2}}%
  \ifdim \wd\@tempboxa >\hsize
    #1{#2}\par
  \else
    \hbox to\hsize{\hfil\box\@tempboxa\hfil}%
  \fi
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip
}
\makeatother
```
This redefines how captions are formatted, making them left-aligned.

### **Method 3: Force Left Alignment with `\raggedright`**
Alternatively, you can use `\raggedright` inside a group:
```latex
\begin{table}[h]
  \centering
  \begin{tabular}{l c r}
    Left & Center & Right \\
    1 & 2 & 3 \\
  \end{tabular}
  \begingroup\raggedright
  \caption{This is a left-aligned caption.}
  \endgroup
\end{table}
```

### **Best Solution (Without `caption` Package)**
The most reliable method is to redefine `\@makecaption` as in **Method 2** or use `\raggedright` selectively.

Would you like a solution tailored to a specific document class (e.g., `article`, `report`, `book`)?
